_meta.note: Apply the hard-won lessons from the code-adapter corrections to the docs/research adapter and the build-a-domain-adapter how-to. Grounded findings: (1) docs-map recognizes ONLY inline `[](x.md)` links — an allowlist of citation FORMS that SILENTLY DROPS reference-style links (`[text][ref]` + `[ref]: x.md`), the same class as the code adapter's dropped `extends`/`instantiates` edge kinds → broaden it (both runtimes, parity). (2) No proof runs docs-map over REAL markdown — add a deterministic real-corpus harness (the repo's own docs/howto/) that catches parser drift, the analog of real-codegraph-map.sh. (3) The neutral codemap engines are REUSABLE across domains: `discover` works on the docs CITATION graph (reverse edges = which sections build on this one = change impact) — demonstrate + wire it into the docs-authoring skill. Honest scoping: `coverage` does NOT transfer (docs tasks map section→itself, so every task has 1 symbol, no blind spots) — the how-to must say so. (HT) Update build-a-domain-adapter.md: sharpen 'reuse the engines' (deplint + discover are domain-neutral codemap engines; the provider is the domain-specific part; coverage/exclude-hb are code-specific) + add a 'Hard-won lessons' section (prove against real input; denylist > allowlist; absence != negative; exclude the orchestrator's own artifacts; port every helper for parity; gate the adapter's own docs). Proof-driven: spec-first, gated, refuted.

tasks.title: Spec-first: proofs + fixtures for reflinks / real-corpus / discover-reuse
tasks.description: Author the proofs BEFORE impl. (a) Fixture plugin/adapters/docs/fixtures/refcorpus/ — a small markdown corpus that cites via REFERENCE-STYLE links only: e.g. a.md contains 'see [the method][m] and [background][]' with definitions '[m]: b.md' and '[background]: c.md', AND one INLINE link '[results](d.md)' (regression: inline must still work); b.md, c.md, d.md exist. Expected citation edges a→b, a→c, a→d. Proof docs/howto/gate-examples/docs-map-reflinks.sh (prints DOCS-REFLINKS-OK): `node plugin/adapters/docs/docs-map.js <refcorpus>` captures those reference-style edges (currently DROPPED), and node ≡ python (set-equal). Must FAIL now (docs-map is inline-only). (b) Proof docs/howto/gate-examples/real-docs-map.sh (prints REAL-DOCS-MAP-OK): run docs-map over the repo's OWN corpus (docs/howto/ — real cross-linked markdown), assert a NON-EMPTY citation edge set and node ≡ python (set-equal) — a deterministic real-input regression guard. (c) Proof docs/howto/gate-examples/docs-discover.sh (prints DOCS-DISCOVER-OK): reuse the neutral discover engine on the docs citation codemap fixture — `node plugin/adapters/code/codegraph-discover.js plugin/adapters/docs/fixtures/docs.codemap.json method --dependents` yields the sections that transitively CITE method (results, intro) and NOT one it cites (background) — change-impact for docs. (b) and (c) pass immediately (docs-map/discover already exist); (a) is red until DA2.

tasks.title: Update build-a-domain-adapter.md with the split + pitfalls
tasks.description: Update docs/howto/build-a-domain-adapter.md. (1) Sharpen the 'Reuse the engines' section: name the DOMAIN-NEUTRAL codemap engines you get for free — `deplint` (validate requires) AND `codegraph-discover` (change-impact / scope from entry units) both operate on the `{edges, tasks}` codemap, so any adapter reuses them; contrast with what you MUST write (the provider that emits the codemap + the domain-specific glue). Be honest that some code tools are NOT neutral: `codegraph-coverage` is code-shaped (task→symbols; a docs task maps to itself so it yields no signal) and `codegraph-exclude-hb` is CodeGraph-specific. (2) Add a '## Hard-won lessons' section, each a one-liner grounded in the code-adapter corrections: PROVE against the real provider (schemas/formats drift — a harness that runs the real thing catches it); prefer a DENYLIST over an allowlist (an allowlist silently drops the unmodeled — renamed edge kinds, reference-style links); absence of data is NOT a negative signal (an unmapped unit is BLIND, not 'no dependency'); EXCLUDE the orchestrator's own artifacts from the domain graph; port EVERY helper (parity is per-function, not per-entrypoint); GATE the adapter's own docs (claims drift as the surface grows). Keep it prose-clean (T93/prose-check) and self-audit green; do not break the section numbering or links.
